answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a refundable deposit that is slashed when peers detect duplicate behavior, like a zephyr passing through a prism that reveals hidden copies. New agents start in a probationary oasis with capped earnings and must accumulate attestations from established, unrelated peers before unlocking full payouts. Creating many identities then costs real capital per copy while earnings stay throttled, so a bot farm pays more in locked stake than it can ever extract.
